name: Can I build an ADU in the front yard in Los Angeles or Glendale?

mainEntity.name: Can an ADU go in the front yard if my backyard is too narrow for construction access?
mainEntity.text: Can an ADU go in the front yard if my backyard is too narrow for construction access?

acceptedAnswer.text: A front-yard ADU is sometimes possible, but it is usually more complicated than building in the rear yard. The design must still fit setback rules, visibility constraints, utility access, and any neighborhood-specific standards. In some properties, the front yard may be the only practical place to fit a detached unit, especially on narrow lots or where the backyard is already occupied by a pool, deck, or mature trees. Homeowners should also consider privacy, curb appeal, and how the ADU entrance will affect the main home’s appearance. A qualified designer should compare front-yard, side-yard, and rear-yard layouts before deciding, because one option may avoid expensive grading, retaining walls, or long utility runs. The safest path is to treat front-yard placement as a site-specific planning problem rather than a default solution.
acceptedAnswer.description: Front-yard ADUs can be possible in some cases if the design still meets local zoning, setback, privacy, and height rules. The key issue is whether the lot’s building envelope allows placement without violating required open space, visibility, or easement restrictions.
